note: Craniofacial dysmorphism is recognized across cohorts as a cardinal feature of Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome, making high-frequency specific facial features plausible and worthy of detailed cohort evaluation.

evidence.text: Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome is defined by developmental delay, intellectual disability, and craniofacial dysmorphisms; all 6 evaluated patients in this cohort presented with craniofacial anomalies.

source.title: Does It Run in Your Family? Inherited Truncating PSMD12 Variants Broaden the Phenotypic Spectrum of Stankiewicz‐Isidor Syndrome
source.quote: Portraying a completely penetrant condition with inter- and intra-familiar clinical variability, all individuals presented with developmental delay, intellectual disability, craniofacial, and skeletal anomalies.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 24 individuals with PSMD12 alterations, facial dysmorphism is a core component of the syndrome and contributes to making it clinically recognizable despite variable expressivity.

source.title: Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome: expanding the clinical and molecular phenotype
source.quote: We refine the phenotype of STISS and show that it can be clinically recognizable and biochemically diagnosed by a type I interferon gene signature.
